title: Use of a 3D Printer to Make Custom Sleep Masks for Positive Airway Pressure Treatment
brief_summary: This is a small pilot study to look at the feasibility of creating a customized sleep mask for use with Continuous Positive Airway Pressure (CPAP) or other similar treatments for sleep apnea. The participant will have three dimensional (3D) pictures of the face taken by special cameras. The pictures will be sent to a 3D printer and a mask will be created based on the participant's face contours. The participant will use the mask for about 6 months. The study will measure the amount it is used during sleep and if there is an increase in reported comfort.
raw_criteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

* On stable NIV settings for a minimum of 2 months.

Exclusion Criteria:

* New diagnosis
